items: Original Chaos
Gaia and Ouranos generate the Titans
Kronos becomes king by castrating his father
Zeus defeats the Titans with lightning

quiz.question: How was the goddess Athena born?
quiz.explanation: For fear of a son more powerful than him, Zeus swallows his pregnant wife Metis: Athena is then born fully armed, emerging from her skull.
options: Zeus swallows the goddess Metis, and Athena emerges fully armed from her skull
She is born from the foam of the sea
She is the daughter of Cronus
She is born from the blood of Ouranos

quiz.question: In which text does the poet Hesiod recount the birth of the Greek gods?
quiz.explanation: Hesiod recounts in the Theogony, in the 8th century BCE, how the world passes from Chaos to the court of Zeus.

quiz.question: True or false: the French word “panic” comes from the god Pan, whose cry is said to have caused sudden terror.
quiz.explanation: During a war against the Giants, the cry of the god Pan would have caused irrational terror among the enemies, hence the word "panic".

title: Prometheus, the fire thief
description: Prometheus stole fire from the gods and gave it to humans, then endured an endless torture. A myth about progress, cunning, and the price of freedom.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Who is punished by Zeus for giving fire to men?
quiz.explanation: Prometheus steals the fire from Olympus to give it to men, an act that Zeus does not forgive.

quiz.question: True or false: during the sacrifice at Mekoné, it is Prometheus who deceives Zeus by hiding the good meat under an ugly skin.
quiz.explanation: Prometheus hides the meat under unappetizing skin and the bones under tempting fat, causing Zeus to choose the wrong part.

quiz.question: Where does Prometheus hide the spark stolen from Olympus?
quiz.explanation: Prometheus steals a spark and hides it in a ferrule rod, the pith of which burns very slowly.

quiz.question: Which animal devours the liver of Prometheus chained in the Caucasus every day?
quiz.explanation: Zeus condemns Prometheus to have his liver devoured by an eagle every day, on the rock of the Caucasus.

quiz.question: True or false: Prometheus' liver grows back every night, making his torment endless.
quiz.explanation: Every night the organ is reborn, so that the torture begins again at dawn, indefinitely.

quiz.question: Which hero finally frees Prometheus from his chains?
quiz.explanation: Heracles, son of Zeus, kills the eagle with an arrow and frees Prometheus from the Caucasus.

quiz.question: What secret does Prometheus reveal to Zeus in exchange for his freedom?
quiz.explanation: Prometheus reveals that the nymph Thetis could give birth to a son more powerful than Zeus, who thus avoids his own downfall.
options: The name of the nymph whose son is said to be more powerful than Zeus
The location of a hidden treasure
The way to definitively defeat the Titans
The formula to become mortal again

quiz.question: Put these stages of the myth of Prometheus in order.
quiz.explanation: From the ruse of sacrifice to the theft of fire, then to torture and liberation, the myth of Prometheus follows a clear progression.
items: Prometheus deceives Zeus during the sacrifice at Mekone
Prometheus steals the fire of Olympus for men
Prometheus is chained in the Caucasus and delivered to the eagle
Heracles frees Prometheus from his chains

title: Pandora and the box
description: The first woman made by the gods, Pandora opened a jar full of plagues. Hope stayed at the bottom. A myth about curiosity and misfortune.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Who made Pandora on the orders of Zeus?
quiz.explanation: Zeus orders Hephaestus, god of the forge, to mold Pandora from clay and water.

quiz.question: Which god offers Pandora trickery and lies?
quiz.explanation: Hermes, messenger of the gods, slips cunning and lies among the gifts of Pandora.

quiz.question: True or false: Epimetheus refuses Zeus' gift, as his brother Prometheus had recommended to him.
quiz.explanation: Despite Prometheus' warning, Epimetheus falls under Pandora's spell and welcomes her.

quiz.question: What did Pandora's container actually contain, according to the original Greek texts?
quiz.explanation: The original account speaks of a "pithos", a large storage jar, not a box.
options: A pithos, a large storage jar

quiz.question: Where does the error come from that transformed Pandora's jar into a “box”?
quiz.explanation: When translating Hesiod, Erasmus of Rotterdam confused “pithos” (jar) and “pyxis” (small box).
options: A confusion of Erasmus of Rotterdam in the 16th century
A mistake made by Hesiod himself

quiz.question: What is left alone at the bottom of the jar, once all the evils are gone?
quiz.explanation: Only Elpis, Hope, remains clinging to the bottom of the jar after the plagues have fled.

quiz.question: True or false: in Hesiod, Pandora is presented as a benevolent gift intended to make men happy.
quiz.explanation: Pandora is conceived as a “beautiful evil”, a punishment intended to strike humanity, not as a benevolent gift.

quiz.question: Put these stages of the Pandora myth in order.
quiz.explanation: From its creation to the fatal opening of the jar, the myth of Pandora follows a very precise progression.
items: The gods make Pandora on the orders of Zeus
Epimetheus welcomes Pandora despite Prometheus' warning
Pandora lifts the lid of the jar
Only Hope remains locked at the bottom

title: Demeter and Persephone
description: Hades carries Persephone off. Her mother Demeter, goddess of the harvest, lets the earth starve. A myth built to explain the seasons.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Who kidnaps Persephone to take her to the Underworld?
quiz.explanation: Hades, king of the underworld, appears on his chariot and carries away Persephone with the secret agreement of Zeus.

quiz.question: What does Demeter do when she learns of her daughter's kidnapping?
quiz.explanation: Inconsolable, Demeter forbids the earth from germinating, which causes a famine threatening humans.
options: She stops the land from producing, causing a famine
She asks Zeus to kill her
She takes refuge on Olympus without reacting
She transforms Hades into a monster

quiz.question: What trap does Hades use to keep Persephone bound to the Underworld?
quiz.explanation: Whoever eats in the realm of the dead belongs to him: Hades offers pomegranate seeds to Persephone before her departure.
options: He makes her eat pomegranate seeds
He offers her a poisoned apple
He gives her a magic ring
He makes her drink a forgetting potion

quiz.question: True or false: because of the pomegranate seeds, Persephone must now spend part of each year in the Underworld.
quiz.explanation: A compromise is necessary: ​​Persephone shares the year between Hades and her mother Demeter.

quiz.question: Which god does Zeus send to demand the return of Persephone?
quiz.explanation: Zeus sends Hermes, messenger of the gods, to demand the return of Persephone to Hades.

quiz.question: How does the myth explain the arrival of autumn and winter?
quiz.explanation: Persephone's departure to Hades pushes Demeter to withdraw her grace from crops: it is autumn and winter.
options: When Persephone returns to the Underworld, Demeter withdraws her grace from nature
When Zeus gets angry with men
When Hades punishes the earth in revenge
When Demeter goes on a trip to Olympus

quiz.question: What are the Eleusinian Mysteries?
quiz.explanation: During her wanderings, Demeter stops at Eleusis, where secret rites are born promising initiates a better fate in the afterlife.
options: Secret rites born from Demeter's passage to Eleusis, promising hope after death
A temple built by Hades for Persephone
A party celebrating the kidnapping of Persephone
A tribunal judging the souls of the dead

quiz.question: Put these stages of the myth of Demeter and Persephone in order.
quiz.explanation: From the kidnapping to the division of the year, this myth explains the alternation of the seasons.
items: Persephone's kidnapping by Hades
The famine caused by Demeter's grief
Persephone eats pomegranate seeds in the Underworld
The division of the year between Hades and Demeter

title: Orpheus and Eurydice
description: Orpheus goes down to the underworld to bring Eurydice back. His music bends death itself. One forbidden glance is enough to lose everything.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Who offers his lyre to Orpheus?
quiz.explanation: Orpheus' lyre is a gift from Apollo, god of the arts.

quiz.question: How does Eurydice die?
quiz.explanation: On the wedding day, Eurydice flees the shepherd Aristaeus, steps on a snake and dies from the venom.
options: Bitten by a snake while fleeing the shepherd Aristaeus

quiz.question: True or false: Orpheus' music manages to put Cerberus to sleep and to weaken Charon, the boatman of the dead.
quiz.explanation: Without weapons, Orpheus crosses the Underworld solely thanks to his music, which puts Cerberus to sleep and softens Charon.

quiz.question: What condition does Hades impose on Orpheus to let Eurydice go back up?
quiz.explanation: Hades accepts Eurydice's return on the condition that Orpheus walks in front of her without turning around before the light.
options: Don't turn around until you reach the light
Go back in a single night

quiz.question: True or false: Orpheus turns towards Eurydice before being taken out of the Underworld, which makes her return definitively to the world of the dead.
quiz.explanation: Near the exit, doubt prevails: Orpheus turns around, and Eurydice is gripped by darkness forever.

quiz.question: How does Orpheus die at the end of the myth?
quiz.explanation: Orpheus' refusal of any new love provokes the fury of the Maenads, who tear him apart.
options: Torn by the Maenads, priestesses of Dionysus

quiz.question: What religious movement was born from the death of Orpheus?
quiz.explanation: From the death of Orpheus was born Orphism, a religious movement promising the salvation of the soul through purification rites.

quiz.question: Put these stages of the myth of Orpheus and Eurydice in order.
quiz.explanation: From the marriage to the definitive loss of Eurydice, this myth follows a tragic and precise plot.
items: Orpheus marries the nymph Eurydice
Eurydice dies bitten by a snake
Orpheus charms the Underworld with his music to bring it back
Orpheus turns around and loses Eurydice forever

title: Narcissus and Echo
description: Echo can only repeat. Narcissus loves nothing but his reflection. Two fates that never manage to meet, and that gave us the word narcissism.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Why does Hera punish the nymph Echo?
quiz.explanation: Echo held Hera back with endless conversations while Zeus joined other nymphs.
options: She had helped Zeus hide his infidelities by distracting her with long conversations
She had stolen a sacred object from Olympus
She refused to marry a god

quiz.question: What punishment does Hera inflict on Echo?
quiz.explanation: Echo can no longer start a sentence: she can only repeat the last words of others.
options: She can only repeat the last words of others
She is banished from the forest

quiz.question: How does Narcissus react when Echo tries to hug him?
quiz.explanation: When Echo approaches to hug her, Narcisse rejects her with contempt.
options: He immediately falls in love with her
He turns her into a flower

quiz.question: True or false: after Narcissus' rejection, Echo's body withers until only a voice is left.
quiz.explanation: Humiliated, Echo retreats into the caves, stops eating and her body withers until only a wandering voice is left.

quiz.question: Which goddess is asked to punish Narcissus for his cruelty?
quiz.explanation: A victim of Narcissus prays to Nemesis, goddess of just revenge, so that he can suffer an impossible love.

quiz.question: What does Narcissus fall in love with at the edge of a spring?
quiz.explanation: Narcissus leans into a spring, discovers its face and falls in love with it, believing he sees a water spirit.

quiz.question: True or false: the soothsayer Teiresias predicted that Narcissus would live a long life if he never knew himself.
quiz.explanation: Teiresias had warned Narcissus' mother: "He will live to be old if he does not know himself."

quiz.question: What is born in place of Narcissus' body after his death?
quiz.explanation: In place of the missing body of Narcissus grows a flower with a yellow heart and white petals, the narcissus.

title: Icarus and Daedalus
description: Daedalus builds wings of wax to escape Crete. His son Icarus flies too high, falls, and gives his name to a sea. A myth about measure and excess.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Why does Minos lock Daedalus and Icarus in the Labyrinth?
quiz.explanation: When Minos learns that Daedalus helped Theseus escape using Ariadne's thread, he locks the inventor and his son in their own work.
options: Because Daedalus helped Theseus escape thanks to Ariadne's thread
Because Daedalus refused to build the Labyrinth
Because Daedalus betrayed the king to an enemy

quiz.question: What materials does Daedalus make the wings with?
quiz.explanation: While observing birds, Daedalus makes wings out of wood, feathers and beeswax.

quiz.question: What advice does Daedalus give to Icarus before leaving?
quiz.explanation: Daedalus recommends the middle path: too low, the humidity weighs down the feathers, too high, the sun melts the wax.
options: Follow a middle path, neither too high nor too low
Fly as high as possible to avoid humidity

quiz.question: What happens when Icarus flies too close to the sun?
quiz.explanation: Fascinated by the sky, Icarus rises too high: the wax softens, the feathers fall and he plunges into the sea.
options: The wax on its wings melts and the feathers fall off
His eyes are blinded by the light
He is struck by Zeus' lightning

quiz.question: True or false: the sea where Icarus fell still bears the name of the Icarian Sea today.
quiz.explanation: The currents carry Icarus' body to an island named Ikaria, and the surrounding sea becomes the Icarian Sea.

quiz.question: Where does Daedalus find refuge after the death of his son?
quiz.explanation: Daedalus reaches Sicily alone and offers his wings to the god Apollo, swearing never to fly again.

quiz.question: How does the painter Bruegel the Elder represent the fall of Icarus in his painting?
quiz.explanation: In Bruegel's painting, the fall of Icarus is only a detail: the world continues without stopping for a hero.
options: Like an almost invisible detail, while the plowman continues his task
As a central and spectacular event
In black and white to highlight the tragedy
With the gods crying in the sky

quiz.question: Put these stages of the myth of Icarus and Daedalus in order.
quiz.explanation: From the construction of the Labyrinth to the fall of Icarus, the story follows a precise progression.
items: Daedalus builds the Labyrinth for King Minos
Minos locks Daedalus and Icarus in their own work
Daedalus makes wings of wood, feathers and wax
Icarus flies too close to the sun and falls into the sea

title: Sisyphus: eternal punishment
description: Sisyphus cheats Death, then the gods themselves. His sentence: roll a rock that always falls back. Camus turned him into the symbol of clear sight in the face of the absurd.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: What secret does Sisyphus reveal, angering Zeus?
quiz.explanation: Sisyphus sells the secret of Zeus's kidnapping of Aegina to the river god Asopos, in exchange for a source of water.
options: He reveals to the river god Asopos that Zeus has kidnapped his daughter Aegina
It reveals the location of the Labyrinth
He reveals a plot against Zeus
He is trying to steal the throne of Olympus

quiz.question: How does Sisyphus manage to imprison Thanatos, Death personified?
quiz.explanation: Sisyphus asks Thanatos for a demonstration of his chains, then actually chains him.
options: He feigns admiration for her chains and asks her for a demonstration, then chains her
He puts her to sleep with a potion
He traps him in the Labyrinth
He trades his own life for his freedom

quiz.question: True or false: while Thanatos is chained by Sisyphus, no one can die on Earth.
quiz.explanation: With Death in chains, even the soldiers of Ares can no longer fall in battle.

quiz.question: What excuse does Sisyphus use to get three days on Earth after his death?
quiz.explanation: Sisyphus complains to Persephone that he has been disgraced by the lack of a funeral, and is granted three days on Earth.
options: He complains to Persephone that his wife didn't give him a funeral.
He claims to have forgotten a treasure
He asks to see his children again
He claims to have been kidnapped by mistake

quiz.question: Which god finally brings Sisyphus back to the Underworld by force?
quiz.explanation: Hermes, messenger of the gods and conductor of souls, brings Sisyphus back to Hades by force.

quiz.question: What is the eternal punishment of Sisyphus?
quiz.explanation: Sisyphus is condemned to push a rock to the top of a hill, but the stone comes back down just short of the goal.
options: Pushing a rock that comes back down just before reaching the top
Carry the sky on your shoulders
Having your liver devoured every day by an eagle
Stay immersed in water without being able to drink

quiz.question: According to Albert Camus in “The Myth of Sisyphus”, what makes him an “absurd hero”?
quiz.explanation: For Camus, Sisyphus' lucidity in the face of the uselessness of his effort, and the fact of continuing despite everything, makes him grow.
options: He continues his effort knowing perfectly well that it is in vain
He secretly hopes that the gods will tire
He completely ignores the vanity of his task
He now refuses to push the rock

quiz.question: True or false: unlike Prometheus, Sisyphus is physically injured every day by his punishment.
quiz.explanation: Sisyphus is not injured in his flesh: his torture is the uselessness of his effort, not physical pain.

quiz.question: Put these stages of the myth of Sisyphus in order.
quiz.explanation: From the revelation of the secret of Aegina to eternal condemnation, the myth of Sisyphus follows a clear progression.
items: Sisyphus reveals to Asopos that Zeus has kidnapped his daughter
Sisyphus chains Thanatos, Death personified
Sisyphus gets three days on Earth and refuses to return
Sisyphus is condemned to push a rock for eternity

title: Tantalus and his torment
description: Tantalus serves his own son to the gods. His sentence: water and fruit forever out of reach. A myth of frustration that even named a chemical element.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Why does Tantalus kill and serve his own son Pelops to the gods?
quiz.explanation: Tantalus invites the gods to a banquet and serves them his severed son, to see if they will notice the deception.
options: To test if the gods really see everything
Out of jealousy towards his son

quiz.question: Which goddess bites off a piece of Pelops' shoulder without meaning to?
quiz.explanation: Demeter, distracted by the grief of her daughter Persephone, is the only one to bite a piece of the dish.

quiz.question: With what does Zeus replace Pelops' eaten shoulder when resurrecting him?
quiz.explanation: Zeus resurrects Pelops and replaces the eaten shoulder with a piece of ivory.

quiz.question: What does the torture of Tantalus in Tartarus consist of?
quiz.explanation: Immersed in a lake and surrounded by fruit, Tantalus sees water and food disappear every time he tries to reach them.
options: He has water and fruit before his eyes, without ever being able to reach them
He must push a rock endlessly
An eagle eats his liver every day
He carries the sky on his shoulders

quiz.question: True or false: as soon as Tantalus tilts his head to drink, the water from the lake sinks into the ground.
quiz.explanation: It is not the absence of water that tortures Tantalus, but its deceptive proximity: it sinks as soon as it approaches.

quiz.question: What chemical element is named after this myth?
quiz.explanation: In 1802, chemist Anders Ekeberg named a new metal “tantalum” in reference to the thirsty king of myth.

quiz.question: Why did the chemist Ekeberg choose this name for the metal he discovered?
quiz.explanation: The metal resists acids without absorbing them, just as Tantalus can never drink the water around it.
options: Because the metal, immersed in acids, absorbs almost none of it
Because the metal is mined near Lydia
Because metal is as heavy as Sisyphus' rock
Because metal changes color on contact with water

quiz.question: True or false: Tantalus' lineage, the Atrides, remains cursed for several generations after this crime.
quiz.explanation: The curse is transmitted to Atrides, which Agamemnon and Orestes will later inherit.

title: Medusa and Perseus
description: Medusa turns anyone who looks at her to stone. Perseus beats her with a mirrored shield, then saves Andromeda. The head of the Gorgon becomes a protective symbol.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: What happens to Medusa after being raped by Poseidon in the temple of Athena?
quiz.explanation: According to ancient tragic logic, Athena punishes the victim: Medusa's hair becomes snakes and her gaze petrifies.
options: Athena transforms her into a monster, her hair becoming snakes
Poseidon marries her and makes her a goddess
It becomes immortal without further change
She is simply banished without punishment

quiz.question: What power does Medusa's gaze have?
quiz.explanation: Medusa's gaze turns anyone who meets it into stone.
options: He petrifies anyone who meets him

quiz.question: What challenge does King Polydectes impose on Perseus?
quiz.explanation: Polydectes wants to send Perseus away to seduce his mother Danae and imposes this suicidal challenge on him.
options: Bring back the head of Medusa

quiz.question: How does Perseus manage to cut off Medusa's head without being petrified?
quiz.explanation: Guided by the reflection of his shield offered by Athena, Perseus cuts off the head of the sleeping Medusa without ever looking at her directly.
options: He only looks at her through the reflection of his polished bronze shield
He fights with his eyes closed
He attacks him at night, while he sleeps, without any particular precautions.
It is protected by an Aphrodite charm

quiz.question: Who offers Perseus the decisive mirror shield?
quiz.explanation: Athena gives Perseus her polished bronze shield, to use as a mirror against Medusa.

quiz.question: What springs from Medusa's neck when Perseus decapitates her?
quiz.explanation: Medusa was pregnant with Poseidon: from her neck sprang Pegasus and the giant Chrysaor.
options: The winged horse Pegasus and the giant Chrysaor

quiz.question: Why is Andromeda chained to a rock when Perseus discovers her?
quiz.explanation: Andromeda is offered to the sea monster Cetos, sent by Poseidon to punish the pride of his mother Cassiopeia.
options: She is offered as a sacrifice to a sea monster to punish her mother's pride
She disobeyed her father the king

quiz.question: What happens to Medusa's head once it is given to Athena?
quiz.explanation: Athena fixes the head of Medusa on her aegis: this Gorgoneion becomes a protective power, adorning temples and shields.
options: It is fixed on its aegis and becomes the Gorgoneion, protective symbol
It is destroyed to erase the memory of Medusa
She is buried at the top of Olympus
She is offered to Poseidon as repair

quiz.question: Put these stages of the myth of Medusa and Perseus in order.
quiz.explanation: From Medusa's attack to Andromeda's deliverance, the story follows a precise progression.
items: Poseidon attacks Medusa in the temple of Athena
Perseus receives magical weapons from the gods for his quest
Perseus cuts off Medusa's head thanks to the reflection of his shield
Perseus frees Andromeda from the sea monster Ketos

title: Hercules and his 12 labors
description: Heracles, son of Zeus, kills his own family in a fit of madness. His Twelve Labors are a penance: kill monsters, then defeat death itself.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Why does Heracles have to perform his twelve labors?
quiz.explanation: Stricken with madness by Hera, Heracles massacres his wife Megara and his children; the works are his penance for this crime.
options: As penance after killing his wife and children in a fit of madness provoked by Hera
To prove his strength to the gods of Olympus
On direct order from Zeus, for no specific reason

quiz.question: Who imposes on Heracles the list of his works?
quiz.explanation: The oracle of Delphi orders Heracles to serve his cousin Eurystheus, who imposes ten labors on him, then twelve.
options: King Eurystheus, his cousin, by order of the oracle of Delphi

quiz.question: How does Heracles defeat the Nemean Lion?
quiz.explanation: Faced with the lion's impenetrable skin, Heracles strangles it with his bare hands, then wears it as armor.
options: He strangles him with his bare hands, his skin being impenetrable to weapons
He drowns him in a river
He traps him in a net

quiz.question: What particularity makes the Lernaean Hydra so difficult to defeat?
quiz.explanation: Each severed head of the Hydra regrows two, until Heracles cauterizes the necks with fire.
options: For every head cut off, two grow back

quiz.question: How does Heracles clean the Augean Stables in a single day?
quiz.explanation: Heracles diverts the rivers Alpheus and Peneus, whose current carries away the manure in a single day.
options: He diverts the course of two rivers through the stables
He uses an army of slaves
It burns all the accumulated manure

quiz.question: How does Heracles manage to bring back the golden apples from the Hesperides?
quiz.explanation: Heracles tricks the titan Atlas to obtain the golden apples of the Hesperides.
options: He tricks the titan Atlas, who carries the sky on his shoulders
He fights a dragon alone in an orchard
He steals apples at night without being seen
He buys them from the guardian nymphs

quiz.question: What is the last and most terrible of the twelve labors of Heracles?
quiz.explanation: Bringing Cerberus back alive from the Underworld symbolizes, for Heracles, a victory over death itself.
options: Descend into Hell and bring back Cerberus

quiz.question: True or false: Heracles dies poisoned by a tunic soaked in the blood of the centaur Nessus, offered by his wife Deianira.
quiz.explanation: Deianira makes Heracles wear a tunic soaked in the poisonous blood of the centaur Nessus, which burns him alive.

quiz.question: What happens after Heracles dies at the stake on Mount Oeta?
quiz.explanation: At the stake, the mortal part of Heracles burns while his divine essence ascends towards Olympus: it is the apotheosis.
options: Its divine part joins Olympus: it is the apotheosis
It only becomes a constellation in the sky
He is reborn immortal on Earth

quiz.question: Put these stages of the myth of Heracles in order.
quiz.explanation: From the madness provoked by Hera to the descent into the Underworld, the labors of Heracles follow a clear progression.
items: Hera drives Heracles crazy and makes him kill his family
Heracles strangles the Nemean Lion with his bare hands
Heracles diverts two rivers to clean the Augean stables
Heracles descends to the Underworld to bring back Cerberus

title: Theseus and the Minotaur
description: Theseus kills the Minotaur thanks to Ariadne's thread. But he forgets to change the sails: his father Aegeus throws himself into the sea, which still carries his name.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Why was the Minotaur born, according to the myth?
quiz.explanation: Minos refuses to sacrifice a white bull to Poseidon, who takes revenge by inspiring Queen Pasiphaé with a passion for the animal, from which the Minotaur is born.
options: Poseidon punishes Minos by instilling in Queen Pasiphae a passion for a bull
Minos deliberately creates a monster to frighten Athens
The Minotaur is a gift from Zeus to Minos
Daedalus invents the Minotaur to test his Labyrinth

quiz.question: Who built the Labyrinth intended to enclose the Minotaur?
quiz.explanation: King Minos commissions the inventor Daedalus to build a dead-end prison, the Labyrinth.

quiz.question: What should Athens deliver to Crete every nine years?
quiz.explanation: After a lost war, Athens must hand over seven young men and seven young girls every nine years as food to the Minotaur.
options: Seven young men and seven young girls grazing with the Minotaur
A tribute of gold and silver
The son of King Aegeus only

quiz.question: Thanks to what object does Theseus manage to get out of the Labyrinth?
quiz.explanation: Ariane gives him a ball of wool which he unrolls as he walks forward, then rewinds to find the exit.
options: A ball of thread that Ariane gave him
A map engraved on the walls

quiz.question: True or false: Theseus abandons the sleeping Ariadne on the island of Naxos during the return trip.
quiz.explanation: On the island of Naxos, Theseus abandons the sleeping Ariadne; some say the god Dionysus wanted her as his wife.

quiz.question: Why did King Aegeus throw himself from Cape Sounion?
quiz.explanation: Theseus forgets to hoist the agreed white sails; seeing the black sails, Aegeus thinks his son is dead and throws himself from the cliff.
options: He thinks his son is dead when he sees the black sails of the ship
He learns of his wife's death

quiz.question: Where does the name of the Aegean Sea come from?
quiz.explanation: The sea has been called Aegean since the king threw himself into it, believing his son to be dead.
options: Of King Aegeus, who died by throwing himself into its waters
From a sea goddess named Aegeus

quiz.question: Once king of Athens, what great political work is attributed to Theseus?
quiz.explanation: Theseus is credited with synoeicism, the unification of the villages of Attica around Athens, as well as the institution of the Panathenaea.
options: The unification of the towns of Attica around Athens (synoecism)

quiz.question: Put these stages of the myth of Theseus and the Minotaur in order.
quiz.explanation: Minos' refusal triggers the birth of the Minotaur, then the tribute, Ariadne's ruse, and finally the death of Aegeus by mistake.
items: Minos refuses to sacrifice a white bull to Poseidon
Theseus volunteers for the tribute sent to Crete
Ariadne gives Theseus the thread that will allow him to escape the Labyrinth
Aegeus throws himself from Cape Sounion seeing the black sails

title: Odysseus and the Cyclops
description: In the Odyssey, Odysseus faces the Cyclops Polyphemus. His [[metis]] saves him, but his pride draws down the anger of Poseidon.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Who is Polyphemus?
quiz.explanation: Polyphemus is a Cyclops, a one-eyed giant, son of the sea god Poseidon.
options: A Cyclops, son of the god Poseidon
A Greek king allied with Odysseus

quiz.question: What sacred Greek rule does Odysseus hope to see respected when he enters the Cyclops' cave?
quiz.explanation: The Greeks believed in xenia, the sacred duty of welcoming the stranger under the protection of Zeus; Polyphemus is completely unaware of this.
options: Xenia, the duty to welcome the stranger

quiz.question: What cunning name does Odysseus give to Polyphemus?
quiz.explanation: Odysseus introduces himself as “Nobody” (Outis in Greek), a name that also evokes mētis — cunning — and sows confusion after the attack.

quiz.question: How do Odysseus and his men manage to wound Polyphemus?
quiz.explanation: Odysseus cuts an olive-wood stake, heats it, then his men drive it into the one eye of the Cyclops, who has been put to sleep by the wine.
options: They drive a burning olive stake into his one eye
They attack him with swords while he sleeps
They cause the cave to collapse

quiz.question: True or false: when the other Cyclops ask who is attacking Polyphemus, he answers "No one", and they walk away without intervening.
quiz.explanation: Polyphemus shouts that “No one” is attacking him: the other Cyclops, believing in divine evil, do not come to help him.

quiz.question: How do Odysseus and his companions get out of the cave watched by the blind Cyclops?
quiz.explanation: Odysseus ties his companions under the wooliest sheep and hangs under the biggest ram himself, so the blind Cyclops will miss them.
options: Hidden under the bellies of the sheep of the flock
By pretending to be painted sheep
By putting Polyphemus to sleep a second time

quiz.question: What mistake does Odysseus make once he is safe at sea?
quiz.explanation: Out of desire for kleos, the glory that survives in name, Odysseus shouts his identity to Polyphemus, who can then curse him by name to Poseidon.
options: He reveals his true name and his city to Polyphemus out of desire for glory.
He abandons some of his men on the island
He refuses to help his injured companions

quiz.question: What is the consequence of Polyphemus' curse on Odysseus?
quiz.explanation: Polyphemus prays to his father Poseidon that Odysseus will wander a long time and lose all his companions: that curse opens ten years of trials at sea.
options: It means ten years of wandering at sea for Odysseus
It turns Odysseus into a Cyclops
It immediately kills all his companions
It keeps Odysseus from ever seeing Ithaca again

quiz.question: Put these stages of the Cyclops episode in order.
quiz.explanation: From the entry into the cave to the blinding, then to the confession of the name at sea, the episode follows a precise progression which seals the fate of Odysseus.
items: Odysseus and his men enter Polyphemus' cave
Polyphemus gets drunk and asks the name of his guest
The Greeks blind the Cyclops with the burning stake
Odysseus shouts his real name from the ship

title: Odysseus and the Sirens
description: The Sirens promise absolute knowledge. Odysseus is the only mortal who hears their song and lives, thanks to a trick that became a model of self-control.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: What do the Sirens promise to those who listen to them?
quiz.explanation: The Sirens promise absolute knowledge, including everything that happened in the Trojan War, the supreme temptation for Odysseus.
options: Absolute knowledge of everything that happens on earth

quiz.question: True or false: in Homer, the Sirens are represented as women with fish tails.
quiz.explanation: In Homer, the Sirens are half-women, half-birds; the representation as a fish woman only appears later, in the Middle Ages.

quiz.question: What does Odysseus do so that his companions do not hear the song of the Sirens?
quiz.explanation: Odysseus plugs the ears of his companions with beeswax so that they hear nothing of the song.
options: He plugs their ears with beeswax
He lands them before the island of the Sirens

quiz.question: How does Odysseus manage to hear the song without succumbing to it?
quiz.explanation: Odysseus gets himself tied to the mast and orders his men to tighten his bonds if he demands his freedom, whatever he says.
options: He is tied to the mast with orders to tighten his bonds if he asks to be released.
He half covers his own ears
He closes his eyes during the entire crossing
He makes his men carry a magic shield

quiz.question: Who warned Odysseus of the danger and the strategy to adopt against the Sirens?
quiz.explanation: The sorceress Circe warned Odysseus and showed him how to prepare.

quiz.question: What social science concept illustrates the scene of Odysseus tied to the mast?
quiz.explanation: Knowing he will be weak in the face of temptation, Odysseus limits his own options in advance: that's precommitment.

quiz.question: True or false: once the song is heard, Odysseus remains perfectly calm and never asks to be detached.
quiz.explanation: When the song rises, Odysseus loses his calm and shouts to be untied; only his men, deaf and faithful to the plan, prevent him from giving in.

quiz.question: How did the image of Sirens evolve in the Middle Ages?
quiz.explanation: In the Middle Ages, the Homeric bird-woman became a fish-woman, and the Church read Sirens as symbols of lust.
options: The bird woman becomes a fish woman, a symbol of lust for the Church
They completely disappear from the iconography
They are associated with the god Poseidon

quiz.question: Put these steps from the Sirens episode in order.
quiz.explanation: Circe's warning precedes the material preparation, then the test of the song itself, where only the prior arrangement saves Odysseus.
items: Circe warns Odysseus of the danger of the Sirens
Odysseus covers his companions' ears with wax
Odysseus gets tied to the ship's mast
The song of the Sirens resounds and Odysseus demands his freedom

title: Jason and the Golden Fleece
description: Jason and the Argonauts sail to Colchis to bring back the Golden Fleece. Behind the adventure lies a story of love and betrayal with the sorceress Medea.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Why does Jason go in search of the Golden Fleece?
quiz.explanation: Pelias, who usurped the throne of Iolcos, promises to return it to Jason if he brings back the Golden Fleece guarded by a dragon.
options: His uncle Pelias demands it from him in exchange for the throne he usurped.
The gods exile him to Colchis
He seeks to avenge his father Éson

quiz.question: How does Jason lose a sandal before claiming his throne?
quiz.explanation: Jason helps an old woman cross a stream, actually the goddess Hera in disguise, and loses a sandal in the mud.
options: By helping an old woman, in reality the goddess Hera in disguise, to cross a stream
During a storm on the Argo

quiz.question: Who makes up the crew of the ship Argo, alongside Jason?
quiz.explanation: The Argo takes on board an elite group of Greek heroes, including Heracles, Orpheus, and the twins Castor and Pollux.
options: Heroes like Heracles, Orpheus, Castor and Pollux

quiz.question: How did the Argonauts cross the Symplegades Rocks?
quiz.explanation: Jason releases a dove: the rocks close on its feathers then open, which allows the Argo to barely pass through.
options: Jason releases a dove to test when the rocks open
They go around the rocks by another path
They wait for a moonless night to go unnoticed

quiz.question: What role does Medea play in the conquest of the Golden Fleece?
quiz.explanation: In love with Jason, Medea provides him with an ointment against the fire of bulls, advises a ruse against the warriors born from dragon teeth, then puts the guardian dragon to sleep.
options: She gives Jason a protective ointment and puts the guardian dragon to sleep
She fights the dragon herself with a sword
She convinces her father to give up the Fleece peacefully
She turns Jason into an invincible bull

quiz.question: True or false: to escape Colchis, Medea kills her own brother Absyrtos and scatters his remains at sea to delay their father.
quiz.explanation: Medea kills her brother Absyrtos and scatters his remains at sea; their father Aeetes stops to collect the body, which allows Jason and Medea to flee.

quiz.question: How does Medea take revenge on Pelias, who refuses to cede the throne to Jason?
quiz.explanation: Medea tricks Pelias' daughters into believing that they can rejuvenate their father by cutting him up, which kills him.
options: She tricks her daughters into killing him in the belief that she will make him younger
She delivers him to the dragon of Colchis
She asks Heracles to fight him

quiz.question: Why does Medea finally take revenge on Jason in Corinth?
quiz.explanation: When Jason wants to marry King Creon's daughter, Medea takes revenge by killing her rival with a poisoned dress, then their own children.
options: Jason wants to abandon her to marry King Creon's daughter
Jason refuses to recognize their children
Jason drives her out of Corinth for no reason
Jason reveals his magical secret to the king

quiz.question: Put these steps in the story of Jason and the Golden Fleece in order.
quiz.explanation: From the departure for Iolcos to Medea's final revenge in Corinth, the myth follows a continuous trajectory of conquest then fall.
items: Jason loses a sandal while helping an old woman
The Argo crosses the Roches Symlégades thanks to a dove
Medea puts the dragon to sleep and Jason takes the Fleece
Medea takes revenge for Jason's betrayal in Corinth

title: Achilles: the heel and invulnerability
description: Achilles, the hero of the Iliad, looks unbeatable. One heel, one arrow, and the myth invents the universal metaphor for a fatal weak point.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Who are Achilles' parents?
quiz.explanation: Achilles is the son of the nymph Thetis and the mortal Peleus.
options: The nymph Thetis and the mortal Peleus
The Goddess Hera and King Priam
The nymph Thetis and the god Zeus

quiz.question: Why does Thetis plunge Achilles into the Styx?
quiz.explanation: Thetis plunges Achilles into the Styx, the river of the Underworld, whose water would make his skin impenetrable, to protect him.
options: To make his skin impenetrable and protect him
To purify him before his official birth
To give him the gift of the word of the gods
To put him to sleep before a long trip

quiz.question: Why does the Achilles heel remain vulnerable?
quiz.explanation: By holding him by the heel to immerse him in the Styx, Thetis leaves this area dry, and therefore vulnerable.
options: Thetis holds him by the heel by dipping him in the Styx, which therefore remains dry
Achilles took his foot out of the water out of curiosity
The Styx never touched his feet
A jealous god cursed his heel

quiz.question: Why does Achilles withdraw from the fight before Troy?
quiz.explanation: After Agamemnon takes his captive Briseis, Achilles, offended, withdraws from the fight, which seriously weakens the Greek army.
options: Agamemnon takes his captive Briseis, an affront he does not tolerate
The gods forbid him to fight

quiz.question: What finally brings Achilles back into battle?
quiz.explanation: It is the death of Patroclus, his dearest companion, which pushes Achilles to take up arms again.
options: The death of his companion Patroclus
A promise of wealth from Agamemnon

quiz.question: True or false: after killing Hector, Achilles drags his body behind his chariot, and only King Priam manages to convince him to return it.
quiz.explanation: Achilles drags Hector's body out of anger; it is the nocturnal visit of old King Priam which brings him back to humanity and makes him return the body.

quiz.question: Who shoots the fatal arrow that kills Achilles in the heel?
quiz.explanation: It is Paris, an archer prince little esteemed for his bravery, who shoots the fatal arrow, guided by Apollo, to the heel of Achilles.

quiz.question: What choice would Achilles have had, according to the myth?
quiz.explanation: Achilles would have had the choice between a long and forgotten life and a short but eternally famous life: he chose glory.
options: A long and forgotten life, or a short and glorious life
Become king of Troy or remain a simple soldier
Fight for the Trojans or the Greeks

quiz.question: What does the expression “Achilles heel” mean today?
quiz.explanation: The term “Achilles heel” refers to the hidden flaw in an otherwise strong system or person.
options: The flaw in an otherwise seemingly solid system
An army's last line of defense

quiz.question: Put these stages of Achilles' life in order.
quiz.explanation: From his protection as a child to his death in battle, Achilles' destiny follows a trajectory marked by the glory and fatality of his heel.
items: Thetis plunges baby Achilles into the Styx, holding him by the heel
Achilles withdraws from combat after Agamemnon's affront
Patroclus' death brings Achilles back to the battlefield
Paris reaches Achilles' heel with an arrow guided by Apollo

title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
description: Oedipus saves Thebes by solving the riddle of the Sphinx. Yet this victory of the mind opens the door to the most terrible tragedy of all.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: What is the Sphinx in the Oedipus myth?
quiz.explanation: The Sphinx is a hybrid creature (body of a lion, bust of a woman, wings of a bird, tail of a serpent) which blocks the roads of Thebes and kills those who fail its riddle.
options: A hybrid monster that poses a deadly riddle to passers-by near Thebes
A sea creature sent by Poseidon

quiz.question: Why is Thebes without a real leader when the Sphinx takes over?
quiz.explanation: King Laius has disappeared, killed by an unknown person at a crossroads, leaving the city of Thebes without a legitimate leader.
options: King Laius has disappeared, killed by an unknown person at a crossroads
The city has just been invaded
The throne has always been vacant

quiz.question: What is the question asked by the Sphinx?
quiz.explanation: The Sphinx asks which being has four feet in the morning, two at noon and three in the evening.
options: What being has four feet in the morning, two at noon, three in the evening?
What is the name of the real king of Thebes?
How to defeat a monster without a weapon?

quiz.question: What answer does Oedipus give to the riddle of the Sphinx?
quiz.explanation: Oedipus answers “The Man”: as a child he crawls on all fours, as an adult he walks on two legs, as an old man he leans on a cane.

quiz.question: True or false: as a reward for his victory over the Sphinx, Oedipus receives the crown of Thebes and marries the widowed queen Jocasta.
quiz.explanation: As promised, Oedipus becomes king of Thebes and marries the widowed queen, Jocasta, after defeating the Sphinx.

quiz.question: Why did Oedipus flee Corinth before arriving at Thebes?
quiz.explanation: An oracle had predicted to Oedipus that he would kill his father and marry his mother: he fled Corinth, believing he would escape this fate.
options: An oracle predicted that he would kill his father and marry his mother.
He was fleeing a civil war

quiz.question: What does Apollo reveal when the plague hits Thebes, later in the reign of Oedipus?
quiz.explanation: Apollo reveals that the plague will only end when King Laius's murderer is identified, which launches Oedipus's fatal investigation.
options: The scourge will end when the murderer of Laius is found
The city must sacrifice a royal child
A new monster threatens the city

quiz.question: What tragic truth does Oedipus' investigation ultimately reveal?
quiz.explanation: The investigation reveals that Oedipus killed his own father Laius and married his own mother Jocasta, without knowing it.
options: He himself killed Laius, his father, and married Jocasta, his mother
The Sphinx had lied about the identity of the king

quiz.question: What does Oedipus do when he learns the truth about his destiny?
quiz.explanation: Having become blind by gouging out his eyes, Oedipus finally “sees” the truth about himself; he then wanders, supported by his daughter Antigone.
options: He immediately goes into exile at sea
He abdicates and names Creon king

quiz.question: Put these stages of the Oedipus myth in order.
quiz.explanation: From the flight from Corinth to the tragic revelation of his identity, Oedipus goes through a journey where the victory over the Sphinx precedes his fall.
items: Oedipus flees Corinth to escape a prophecy
Oedipus answers “Man” to the riddle of the Sphinx
Oedipus becomes king of Thebes and marries Jocasta
Plague investigation reveals Oedipus killed his own father

title: Antigone: family duty versus the law of the state
description: Antigone buries her brother against the order of King Creon. Sophocles sets up a conflict that has never gone away: the law of the state, or a higher moral duty?
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Why is Polyneices not entitled to a funeral, according to Creon's decree?
quiz.explanation: Polyneices attacked Thebes with a foreign army; Treated as a traitor, Creon refuses him any burial, unlike his brother Eteocles.
options: He attacked his own city with a foreign army and is treated as a traitor
He died too far from Thebes
He did not belong to the royal family

quiz.question: Why was the absence of a grave so terrifying to the ancient Greeks?
quiz.explanation: For the Greeks, without a funeral rite, the soul of the dead wanders near the Styx, the river of the Underworld, without ever finding rest.
options: Without funeral rites, the soul wanders restlessly near the Styx
The body risks being eaten by sacred animals
It only dishonors the living, not the dead
The city loses its religious status

quiz.question: How does Antigone carry out the funeral rite despite Creon's ban?
quiz.explanation: A simple handful of earth was symbolically enough to complete the funeral rite: it is this discreet gesture that Antigone performs alone.
options: By symbolically covering the body with earth
By calling on the army to protect the body

quiz.question: On what principle does Antigone base her disobedience before Creon?
quiz.explanation: Antigone claims natural law: unwritten and immutable laws, older and more legitimate than the decrees of kings.
options: Unwritten and immutable laws, older than human decrees
Her status as a princess, superior to the laws
A secret order from the gods received in a dream
The promise made to his father Oedipus

quiz.question: What punishment does Creon impose on Antigone?
quiz.explanation: Creon condemns Antigone to be walled up alive for disobeying his decree.
options: The banishment of her sister Ismene with her

quiz.question: True or false: Antigone's sister, Ismene, disobeys with her from the start and buries Polyneices alongside her.
quiz.explanation: Ismene hesitates, cautious, and does not act with Antigone: she performs the forbidden funeral rite alone.

quiz.question: Who is Haemon, and what role does he play in the tragedy?
quiz.explanation: Haemon, son of Creon and fiancé of Antigone, tries in vain to reason with his father before the tragedy occurs.
options: Creon's son and Antigone's fiancé, who tries to reason with his father
A soothsayer who predicted the fall of Thebes

quiz.question: What does the soothsayer Tiresias reveal to Creon?
quiz.explanation: Teiresias announces that the gods are angry: the city is sullied by the abandoned corpse and by the unjust imprisonment of Antigone.
options: The gods are angry with the city sullied by its decisions
Antigone must be released immediately and unconditionally

quiz.question: What deaths occur after Creon's late change of heart?
quiz.explanation: Creon gives in too late: Antigone hangs herself, her son Hémon commits suicide, then Eurydice, Creon's wife, also kills herself.
options: Antigone hangs herself, Haemon and Eurydice commit suicide
Only Antigone dies, the rest of the family survives
Ismene commits suicide in Antigone's place

quiz.question: Put these stages of the tragedy of Antigone in order.
quiz.explanation: From the death of the two brothers to Creon's decree, then to Antigone's disobedience and her condemnation, the tragedy follows inexorably.
items: Eteocles and Polyneices kill each other for the throne of Thebes
Creon forbids any burial for Polyneices
Antigone performs the forbidden funeral rite alone
Creon condemns Antigone to be walled up alive

title: The Trojan War and the wooden horse
description: Ten years of siege, gods on both sides, then a wooden horse. The greatest epic story of ancient Greece, and the model for every military trick since.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: What, according to myth, started the Trojan War?
quiz.explanation: Paris chooses Aphrodite at the judgment of the golden apple; she offers him the love of Helen, wife of Menelaus, which triggers the war.
options: The choice of Paris, who offers the golden apple to Aphrodite and obtains Helen as a reward
A surprise attack by Troy against Sparta
A trade dispute between Greeks and Trojans

quiz.question: Who takes command of the Greek coalition that sets out to besiege Troy?
quiz.explanation: Agamemnon, brother of Menelaus and king of Mycenae, takes command of the Greek fleet that sets out to besiege Troy.
options: Agamemnon, king of Mycenae and brother of Menelaus

quiz.question: Why are the walls of Troy considered almost indestructible?
quiz.explanation: The walls of Troy are said to be indestructible because they were built with the help of the gods Poseidon and Apollo.
options: They were built with the help of Poseidon and Apollo
They are made of a unique sacred metal

quiz.question: Who invented the wooden horse trick?
quiz.explanation: It is Odysseus, master of mētis — intelligent cunning — who invents the wooden-horse trap that brings Troy down.
options: Odysseus, king of Ithaca and master of mētis

quiz.question: How did the Greeks convince the Trojans to accept the horse within their walls?
quiz.explanation: The Greek spy Autre convinces the Trojans that the horse is an offering for Athena, despite the priest Laocoon's warnings.
options: The spy Autre makes them believe that it is an offering for Athena
They officially offer it as a sign of signed peace
They threaten to burn the city otherwise

quiz.question: True or false: the Trojan priest Laocoon warns his compatriots that the horse is a trap, but he is ignored.
quiz.explanation: Laocoon cries trap, but the Trojans ignore him and bring the horse into the city, sealing their fate.

quiz.question: How do the Greek soldiers hidden in the horse end up taking the city?
quiz.explanation: When night came, the soldiers hidden in the horse came out, opened the city gates, and the returned Greek army completed the capture of Troy.
options: They come out at night and open the gates to the returning Greek army
They attack in broad daylight as soon as they arrive
They wait ten more days before acting

quiz.question: What happens to the Trojan prince Aeneas after the fall of the city?
quiz.explanation: Aeneas flees with his father and his gods Lares; Roman legend later made him the founding ancestor of Rome.
options: He fled with his father and his gods, becoming according to legend the ancestor of Rome
He is taken prisoner by Agamemnon
He becomes king of rebuilt Troy

quiz.question: What do the Nostoi, mentioned after the fall of Troy, mean?
quiz.explanation: The Nostoi designate the returns of the Greek victors, often tragic: Agamemnon is assassinated, Odysseus wanders for ten more years.
options: The perilous and often tragic returns of the victorious Greek heroes
The new laws imposed on Troy
The name given to the Trojan survivors
A tribute paid by the Greeks to the gods

quiz.question: Put these stages of the Trojan War in order.
quiz.explanation: From the judgment of Paris to the final ruse of the wooden horse, ten years separate the outbreak of war from the fall of the city.
items: Paris chooses Aphrodite and obtains the love of Helene
The Greek coalition besieges Troy for ten years without a winner
The Greeks build the wooden horse and pretend to leave
Hidden soldiers open the gates of Troy in the night

title: Thor and Loki (Norse mythology)
description: The god of thunder and the god of trickery: partners in adventure, then enemies at Ragnarok. Two faces of the Norse pantheon.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: What is the major source that transmits the myths of Thor and Loki to us?
quiz.explanation: The Prose Edda, written around 1220 by the Icelander Snorri Sturluson and supplemented by the Poetic Edda, is the major source of these myths.
options: The Prose Edda, written by Snorri Sturluson around 1220
A Roman poem from the 1st century
A Christian religious treatise from the 6th century

quiz.question: How is the Nordic world organized, according to mythology?
quiz.explanation: The world is organized around the cosmic tree Yggdrasil: Asgard, home of the gods, above, and Midgard, world of men, lower down, connected by the Bifröst.
options: Around the cosmic tree Yggdrasil, with Asgard above and Midgard below
Around a single ocean with no land surface
On seven superimposed skies without connection between them
Around a unique mountain inhabited by all the gods

quiz.question: What is Thor's role among the Norse gods?
quiz.explanation: Thor is the most revered god of the people: he defends humanity against the giants with his hammer Mjöllnir.
options: He protects humanity against giants with his hammer Mjöllnir
He is the god of trickery and lies
He reigns alone on Nordic Olympus without another god

quiz.question: What is special about Thor's hammer, Mjöllnir?
quiz.explanation: Mjöllnir, forged by dwarves, shatters mountains and always returns to Thor's hand after being thrown.
options: It always returns to Thor's hand after being thrown
It can only be lifted by Odin
It melts on contact with fire

quiz.question: Who is Loki, by his origin?
quiz.explanation: Loki lives among the Aesir but is of giant blood; he joined the pantheon through a blood pact with Odin.
options: A giant blood being integrated into the pantheon of the Aesir by a pact with Odin
A Vane god specializing in fertility
A mere mortal elevated to the rank of god

quiz.question: True or False: Loki can change shape and even gender, and once becomes the mother of Odin's eight-legged horse.
quiz.explanation: Loki changes shape and gender; in the form of a mare, he becomes the mother of Sleipnir, Odin's eight-legged horse.

quiz.question: What monsters does Loki create with the giantess Angrboda?
quiz.explanation: With the giantess Angrboda, Loki creates three monsters: the wolf Fenrir, the serpent Jörmungandr and Hel, guardian of the dead.
options: The wolf Fenrir, the serpent Jörmungandr and Hel

quiz.question: What act of Loki definitively seals his fate as a traitor?
quiz.explanation: By organizing the death of the luminous god Baldr, Loki definitively switches from farce to betrayal, and his fate is sealed.
options: He organizes the death of the luminous god Baldr
He refuses to help the gods against the giants
He reveals a secret of Odin to men

quiz.question: How do Thor and Loki recover the hammer stolen by the giant Thrym?
quiz.explanation: When the giant Thrym steals Mjöllnir, Thor disguises himself as a bride and Loki as a servant to infiltrate his lair and recover the hammer.
options: Thor disguises himself as a bride and Loki as a servant
They directly attack the giant's lair
They send Sleipnir to steal it discreetly

quiz.question: Let's put these stages of Thor and Loki's relationship in order.
quiz.explanation: From Loki's integration into the Aesir to Thor's death at Ragnarök, the comic alliance gradually changes into a fatal confrontation.
items: Loki joins the pantheon of the Aesir through a pact with Odin
Thor and Loki together recover the hammer stolen by the giant Thrym
Loki arranges the death of the god Baldr
Thor kills the serpent Jörmungandr and dies of its venom at Ragnarök

title: Ragnarök: the end of the Norse world
description: Not a divine punishment but a fate the gods accept: the gods of Asgard fall, the world burns, then rises again greener. This is the Norse apocalypse.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: What does the word “Ragnarök” mean more precisely in Old Norse, rather than “twilight of the gods”?
quiz.explanation: The exact meaning of “Ragnarök” is close to “destiny of the powers”; the translation “twilight of the gods” comes from an etymological confusion popularized by Wagner.

quiz.question: True or false: Ragnarök begins with a Great Winter of three years without summer, called Fimbulwinter.
quiz.explanation: Fimbulwinter, a three-year winter without summer that breaks up families, precedes and announces Ragnarök.

quiz.question: Which god is devoured by the wolf Fenrir during the final battle?
quiz.explanation: Odin, father of the gods, is swallowed up by Fenrir on the plain of Vígríðr, before his son Víðarr avenges him.

quiz.question: How does Thor die after crushing the serpent Jörmungandr with Mjölnir?
quiz.explanation: Thor kills Jörmungandr with his hammer Mjölnir, but succumbs to its venom after taking nine steps.
options: He dies poisoned by the snake's venom, after nine steps
He is burned alive by the giant Surtr
He drowns in the flooded ocean
He is devoured by a cosmic wolf

quiz.question: Why does the god Freyr find himself without weapons to face Ragnarök?
quiz.explanation: Freyr had offered his magic sword out of love to marry the giantess Gerd: he therefore died unarmed during Ragnarök.
options: He offered his magic sword out of love to obtain the hand of the giantess Gerd
He lost it in a bet with Loki
It was stolen from him by the serpent Jörmungandr
He never owned a magic sword

quiz.question: Put these stages of Ragnarök in chronological order.
quiz.explanation: From the Great Winter to the rebirth of the earth, Ragnarök follows a precise sequence: warning signs, final battle, conflagration, then renewal.
items: Fimbulwinter, a three-year winter without summer
The wolf Fenrir breaks his chains
The Battle on the Vígríðr Plain
The giant Surtr sets the nine worlds ablaze
The earth turns green again and a new generation of gods survives

quiz.question: Who survives, hidden in the Yggdrasil tree, to repopulate the world after Ragnarök?
quiz.explanation: Líf and Lífþrasir, whose names mean "Life" and "Touch of Life", fed on dew hidden in Yggdrasil and brought humanity back to life.

quiz.question: True or false: after Ragnarök, the earth remains barren and charred forever.
quiz.explanation: On the contrary, once the flames are extinguished, the earth emerges from the waves greener and more fertile than before.

title: Osiris and Set (Egyptian mythology)
description: Murder, dismemberment, a mummy and revenge: the cycle of Osiris and Set founds Egyptian kingship and the hope of a life after death.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: How does Set manage to trap his brother Osiris?
quiz.explanation: At a banquet, Set presents a chest that he will offer to the one who fits inside it perfectly: Osiris lies down on it, and Set seals it before throwing it into the Nile.
options: He invites her to lie down in a magnificent chest made exactly to her size
He poisons her at a banquet
He drowns him directly in the Nile without any prior trap
He challenges him to a duel in court

quiz.question: True or false: after finding the body of Osiris, Set cuts it into fourteen pieces which he scatters in the valley.
quiz.explanation: When Isis finds the body, Set cuts it into fourteen pieces and scatters them to prevent any peace in the afterlife.

quiz.question: Why is Osiris often depicted with green skin?
quiz.explanation: The green of Osiris does not indicate death but rebirth, like the fields that green up after the Nile floods.
options: This color symbolizes plant rebirth, not rot
It designates its belonging to the kingdom of the dead
It recalls the color of the waters of the Nile
It indicates that he is a minor god

quiz.question: Who helps Isis find and reassemble the pieces of Osiris' body?
quiz.explanation: Isis sets out in search of the fragments helped by her sister Nephthys and the god Anubis, erecting a sanctuary at each location found.
options: His sister Nephthys and the god Anubis

quiz.question: What do Isis and Anubis create by gathering the pieces of Osiris' body and wrapping them in strips?
quiz.explanation: By wrapping the reconstituted body in strips, Isis and Anubis create the first mummy in Egyptian tradition.

quiz.question: Put these stages of the myth of Osiris and Set in order.
quiz.explanation: The story follows a clear sequence: the murder of Osiris, his reconstitution by Isis, the hidden youth of Horus, then his coronation after the conflict against Set.
items: Set traps and dismembers the body of Osiris
Isis puts the pieces together and creates the first mummy
Horus grew up in secret in the swamps of Khemmis
Horus is crowned king after his long conflict with Set

quiz.question: True or false: during his conflict with Set, Horus lost an eye which then became an Egyptian symbol of protection.
quiz.explanation: The eye of Horus, recomposed by the god Thoth after this fight, becomes the Oudjat, symbol of healing and protection.

quiz.question: What happens to Osiris once mummified, unable to reign on earth?
quiz.explanation: Mummified, Osiris can no longer reign on earth and becomes sovereign of Amenti, the kingdom of the dead.
options: The ruler of the realm of the dead, Amenti
The god of the Nile and floods
Guardian of the Throne of Horus

quiz.question: During the weighing of the heart described in the Book of the Dead, what happens if the heart of the deceased is heavy with faults?
quiz.explanation: If the heart, weighed against the pen of Ma'at, is heavy with faults, the monster Ammout devours it and the deceased disappears definitively.
options: The monster Ammout devours him, which means definitive oblivion
He must weigh in again the following year
He becomes a servant of Osiris for eternity
He is sent to fight the serpent Apophis

title: Gilgamesh: the first hero in history
description: King of Uruk, friend of Enkidu, hunter of immortality: the Epic of Gilgamesh, written 4,000 years ago, is humanity's oldest great story.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: In what medium has the Epic of Gilgamesh been preserved for over 4,000 years?
quiz.explanation: The text was engraved in cuneiform script on clay tablets, a medium that has survived where papyrus would have disappeared.
options: Clay tablets engraved in cuneiform writing

quiz.question: In what year did the Assyriologist George Smith decipher, at the British Museum, the story of the Flood contained in the epic?
quiz.explanation: George Smith deciphered the Flood Tablet in 1872, revealing a story that predates that of Genesis by about a thousand years.

quiz.question: What does the comparison between the story of the Flood of Gilgamesh and that of biblical Genesis reveal?
quiz.explanation: This story of the Flood precedes the biblical story of Noah by about a thousand years, while sharing the same Mesopotamian cultural background.
options: The story of Gilgamesh predates the biblical story by about a thousand years
The story of Gilgamesh was written after Genesis
The two stories have nothing in common.
The story of Gilgamesh was translated directly from the Greek

quiz.question: Why does the goddess Aruru shape Enkidu?
quiz.explanation: Gilgamesh is an unbearable king for Uruk: Aruru shapes Enkidu, a wild man, to channel him.
options: To create a rival capable of channeling the tyranny of Gilgamesh
To avenge the death of an offended god
To populate the city of Uruk with additional inhabitants

quiz.question: What do Gilgamesh and Enkidu do together, once they become friends?
quiz.explanation: Becoming friends after a fight without a winner, they kill together the monster Humbaba then the Celestial Bull sent by Ishtar.
options: They kill the monster Humbaba then the Celestial Bull
They found a new rival city of Uruk
They immediately leave to find the plant of immortality

quiz.question: True or false: it is the death of his friend Enkidu that pushes Gilgamesh to set out in search of immortality.
quiz.explanation: Faced with Enkidu's corpse, Gilgamesh understands that he will also die and goes to look for Ut-napishti, the only man who has become immortal.

quiz.question: What test does Ut-napishti impose on Gilgamesh to test his ability to conquer death?
quiz.explanation: Gilgamesh immediately falls asleep in the face of this ordeal: he who does not overcome sleep will not overcome death.
options: Stay awake six days and seven nights
Swimming across the Waters of Death
Recite a sacred poem without error

quiz.question: What happens to the plant of youth that Gilgamesh ended up obtaining?
quiz.explanation: While Gilgamesh is bathing, a snake steals the plant of youth and molts immediately after eating it.
options: A snake steals it from him while he is bathing
He eats her too soon and she doesn't do anything
He offers it in vain to Enkidu, already dead.
She dries up before returning to Uruk

quiz.question: What lesson does Gilgamesh ultimately learn from his failure to become immortal?
quiz.explanation: Back in Uruk, Gilgamesh understands that biological immortality belongs to the gods, while man endures through his works and the memory of the living.
options: True immortality lies in the works we leave behind and the memory of the living
You must avoid all friendship to live longer
Immortality is only obtained through prayer

title: Romulus and Remus: the founding of Rome
description: Suckled by a she-wolf, founders of Rome, and killers of a brother. A myth that puts law and the sacred boundary above blood.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: Why does Amulius force his niece Rhea Silvia to become a vestal virgin?
quiz.explanation: By forcing his niece Rhea Silvia to become a vestal, the usurper Amulius seeks to extinguish the line of his brother Numitor.
options: To prevent her from having children who would threaten her usurped power
To honor her as Princess of Alba the Long
Because tradition required it for all princesses
To protect her from an imminent war

quiz.question: Who is the divine father of the twins Romulus and Remus?
quiz.explanation: The god of war Mars unites with Rhea Silvia, who gives birth to the twins Romulus and Remus.

quiz.question: True or false: after being thrown into the Tiber, the twins are taken in and nursed by a she-wolf.
quiz.explanation: The twins' cradle washes up near the Palatine, where a she-wolf breastfeeds them before the shepherd Faustulus raises them.

quiz.question: How do Romulus and Remus try to decide where to found their city?
quiz.explanation: The twins take the omens: Remus sees six vultures first, then Romulus sees twelve.
options: By observing the flight of vultures, according to the practice of omens
By organizing a duel between them

quiz.question: Why does Romulus kill his brother Remus?
quiz.explanation: Romulus had promised death to anyone who crossed the pomoerium, the sacred furrow: Remus crossed it in defiance and Romulus killed him.
options: Remus defiantly crosses the sacred furrow that Romulus had just traced
Remus tries to overthrow him from the throne
Remus wants to marry a Sabine promised to Romulus
Remus refuses to participate in the founding of the city

quiz.question: What date does Roman tradition retain for the founding of Rome?
quiz.explanation: According to tradition, Rome was founded on April 21, 753 BC. BC, starting date of the Roman calendar.

quiz.question: What event pushed the Romans to organize the Rape of the Sabine Women?
quiz.explanation: The city lacking women, Romulus organizes games to attract neighbors and kidnap young Sabine girls.
options: The lack of women in the new city of Rome
A sudden declaration of war by the Sabines

quiz.question: How did the war between the Romans and Sabines, triggered by the Rape of the Sabine Women, end?
quiz.explanation: Sabine women, already mothers of Roman children, intervene on the battlefield: the war ends and the two peoples merge.
options: The Sabine women interpose themselves between their fathers and their husbands, and the two peoples merge
Rome is destroyed and must be refounded

quiz.question: What happened to Romulus, according to the official version of his disappearance during a storm?
quiz.explanation: The official version is that Mars takes Romulus to heaven, where he becomes the god Quirinus, although rumor speaks of an assassination by the senators.
options: He is taken to heaven by Mars and becomes the god Quirinus
He retires to an isolated temple
He is exiled by the Senate

quiz.question: Put these stages of the founding of Rome in order.
quiz.explanation: From the abandoned cradle on the Tiber to the apotheosis of Romulus, the myth follows a precise chronology of the birth, foundation and fusion of peoples.
items: Birth of twins, sons of Mars and Rhea Silvia
A wolf breastfeeds the twins abandoned on the banks of the Tiber
Romulus traces the sacred furrow and kills Remus
The Rape of the Sabines triggers a war then a fusion of peoples
Romulus disappears and becomes the god Quirinus

title: Vishnu and Shiva (Hindu mythology)
description: Create, preserve, destroy in order to be reborn: Vishnu and Shiva, pillars of the Trimurti, keep the cyclical time of Hinduism turning.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: In the Hindu Trimurti, what role does Vishnu play?
quiz.explanation: Vishnu ensures that the order of the world holds, while Brahma creates and Shiva destroys to allow renewal.
options: He creates the universe every cycle
He destroys what is worn out to allow renewal
He judges the souls of the dead

quiz.question: True or false: Brahma, the creator of the universe, is one of the most revered gods in India today.
quiz.explanation: The role of Brahma ends after the creation of each cycle of the universe, which explains why he is little venerated today compared to Vishnu and Shiva.

quiz.question: Why does Vishnu come down to Earth in the form of an avatar?
quiz.explanation: Vishnu protects Dharma, moral and cosmic law, by descending to Earth in avatar form when evil threatens to take over.
options: To protect the Dharma when evil threatens to prevail
To punish men for their sins
To replace Brahma after the creation of the universe

quiz.question: Which of these avatars of Vishnu especially embodies wisdom and divine love?
quiz.explanation: Among the avatars of Vishnu, King Rama embodies virtue, while Krishna embodies wisdom and divine love.

quiz.question: Which avatar of Vishnu is expected to close the Kali Yuga, the last dark age?
quiz.explanation: The tenth avatar, Kalki, will come on a white horse to close the dark age of Kali Yuga.
options: Kalki, riding on a white horse

quiz.question: In what form does Shiva perform his cosmic dance, the Tandava?
quiz.explanation: In the form of Nataraja, "king of dance", Shiva performs the Tandava, holding the rhythm of creation in one hand and the fire of destruction in the other.
options: The solitary ascetic of Mount Kailash

quiz.question: True or false: in the Nataraja statue, one foot of Shiva crushes ignorance while the other, raised, offers liberation.
quiz.explanation: One foot of Nataraja crushes ignorance, the other, raised, offers liberation: change is represented as the only constant.

quiz.question: Who are Shiva's wife and son, despite his image as a solitary ascetic?
quiz.explanation: Shiva is a god of paradoxes: an ascetic covered in ashes on Mount Kailash, but also husband of Parvati and father of Ganesh.

quiz.question: How many billions of years does a “day of Brahma” (a Kalpa) last, according to Hindu tradition?
quiz.explanation: A Kalpa lasts approximately 4.32 billion years, a duration surprisingly close to the age of Earth estimated by modern science.

title: The Valkyries and Valhalla
description: In the Norse sky, warrior women choose the dead who will fill Valhalla. Their army has to face the twilight of the gods.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: What does the name “Valkyrie” literally mean?
quiz.explanation: The name Valkyrie means "those who choose killings", in reference to their role of selection on the battlefields.

quiz.question: Why does Odin bring together the best warriors who died in Valhalla?
quiz.explanation: Odin knows the prophecy of Ragnarök and gathers the Einherjar, an elite army, in Valhalla to delay the inevitable.
options: To build an army for Ragnarök
To offer them a peaceful retirement
To repopulate Asgard after a famine
To judge them for their faults

quiz.question: True or false: all warriors who die in battle automatically join Valhalla.
quiz.explanation: Only half of the warriors who died in battle reach Valhalla; the other half goes to Fólkvangr, domain of the goddess Freyja.

quiz.question: How many gates does Valhalla have, according to Norse texts?
quiz.explanation: Valhalla has 540 gates, each large enough for eight hundred fighters to pass through abreast.

quiz.question: How do ancient texts, such as the Poetic Edda, actually describe the Valkyries, as opposed to the romantic image of the 19th century?
quiz.explanation: The image of gentle virgins comes from 19th century romanticism; ancient texts show harsher figures, linked to crows and sometimes macabre.
options: Like hard figures, linked to crows and sometimes macabre
Like simple servants without any power

quiz.question: What role do the Valkyries play once the heroes arrive in Valhalla?
quiz.explanation: In Valhalla, the Valkyries shed the armor to serve mead to the heroes, recognizing their new status as Asgard's elite.
options: They serve them mead at feasts
They judge them before letting them in
They fight for them every day
They send them back to earth after a year

quiz.question: What is a typical day in Valhalla like for the Einherjar?
quiz.explanation: At the crowing of the cock, the Einherjar arm themselves and kill each other on the plain; in the evening, their wounds close and the feast comes.
options: They fight during the day, their wounds heal, then they celebrate at night
They sleep all day waiting for Ragnarök
They train without ever getting hurt or fighting
They serve Odin as simple servants

quiz.question: True or false: dying of old age or illness, the "straw death", leads to Valhalla just like dying in battle.
quiz.explanation: The Straw Death leads to the dark realm of Hel; only a heroic death, sword in hand, opens the gates of Valhalla.

quiz.question: What final event justifies, according to the myth, all this daily training of the Einherjar in Valhalla?
quiz.explanation: Odin prepares this elite army to face Ragnarök, the final battle that will destroy the world and kill the gods.
options: Ragnarök, the final battle against giants and monsters
An annual tournament organized by Odin
A permanent war against the Vanir

title: The Phoenix across cultures
description: From Egypt to China, the bird that rises from its own ashes travels through civilizations. One shared dream: that destruction is never final.
subject: mythologie

quiz.question: What is the Egyptian ancestor of the Phoenix, often represented as a heron rather than a flaming bird of prey?
quiz.explanation: The Benu, whose name means "to shine" or "to rise", is the Egyptian ancestor of the Phoenix, often represented as a heron.

quiz.question: Which Greek historian transformed the Egyptian Benu into the Phoenix, the bird with red and golden feathers?
quiz.explanation: The Greek historian Herodotus transformed the Benu into the Phoenix, a rare bird with red and gold feathers.

quiz.question: According to Herodotus, every how many years is the Phoenix supposed to reappear?
quiz.explanation: According to Herodotus, the Phoenix reappears every 500 years.

quiz.question: How do the Romans, notably Ovid and Pliny the Elder, describe the end of the Phoenix?
quiz.explanation: The Phoenix builds a nest of spices that the sun or its own wings ignite; from the ashes a young bird is born which carries the remains of its elder to Egypt.
options: He consumes himself in a nest of spices before a young bird is reborn from his ashes.
He dives into the Nile to regenerate
It turns into a sacred stone
It simply disappears without a trace

quiz.question: What does the Phoenix symbolize for the Roman Empire?
quiz.explanation: For Rome, the Phoenix becomes the symbol of Aeternitas, the eternity of the Empire; later, Christians will read the resurrection there.
options: Aeternitas, the eternity of the Empire

quiz.question: How does the Chinese Fenghuang differ from the Greco-Roman Phoenix?
quiz.explanation: The Fenghuang is not a burning bird: it is a creature of harmony, often linked to the empress, whose appearance announces a just sovereign.
options: It is not a bird that burns, but a creature of harmony linked to the empress
